title: correction signals counted DSH-injected user-role records as user pushback

evidence.excerpt: # Handoff: Build `/self-improve` for dshfiles ## Objective Implement a `/self-improve` skill that allows our DSH-based ADE to **learn from its own historical sessions and continuously improve the agent harness, workflows, tools, skills, pro

<system-reminder> The following workspace instructions may be relevant to your work. Use them as guidance when applicable. More specific instructions take precedence over broader ones. They do not override system, developer, or direct user

<system-reminder> A skill is a reusable set of task-specific instructions. The following skills are available in this session: <available_skills> - `actor-state-ownership`: Design frontend state machines and actors with explicit ownership,

rootCause: Prompt origin was guessed from message text and index; DSH marks it structurally in data.source.kind, and appends runtime context, the skill catalog, compaction checkpoints, background-job notices and peer-agent messages as user-role records.
hypothesis: Classifying prompts by data.source.kind (only 'user' is human) and by whether the agent has produced output yet removes the false corrections without losing genuine pushback.

experiments.hypothesis: Classifying a user-role record by its structural origin (data.source.kind; only 'user' is human) and by whether the agent has already produced output removes false correction signals without losing genuine pushback.
experiments.baseline: extractor version 1 over the same 14-day corpus, saved as output/self-improve/baseline-before-fix.json before the change
experiments.metric: Sessions and hits per correction signal, coverage.totalCorrections, and the presence of turn-end:completed
experiments.before: misunderstood-requirement 631 sessions/1943 hits; process-complaint 56/103; incomplete-or-unfixed 631/3979; unwanted-change 70/128; coverage.totalCorrections 4095; turn-end:completed 601/2960
experiments.after: misunderstood-requirement 24/29; process-complaint 2/2; incomplete-or-unfixed 130/188; unwanted-change 23/23; coverage.totalCorrections 224; turn-end:completed not reported
experiments.conditions: Same DSH_HOME and 14-day window, harness unchanged, extractor version 1 to 4. The corpus grew from 806 to 810 analyzed Sessions between the runs, which is why the two control signals drift slightly and why 'after' is not exactly reproducible today.

history.note: Fixed: prompt origin is read from data.source.kind and the opening brief is recognised by whether the agent has produced output yet.

title: turn-end counted normal 'completed' endings as friction
rootCause: The turn-end signal used a denylist that excluded only 'stop' and 'unknown'.

experiments.hypothesis: An allowlist of abnormal turn-end reasons stops normal 'completed' endings being reported as friction.
experiments.baseline: extractor version 1, which kept every reason except 'stop' and 'unknown'
experiments.metric: The turn-end:completed signal's session and hit counts
experiments.before: turn-end:completed 601 sessions/2960 hits, ranked third of 4299 signals
experiments.after: not reported; turn-end:interrupted is unchanged by the fix (100/142 to 97/136 is the corpus moving from 806 to 810 Sessions)
experiments.conditions: Same corpus and window; deterministic, so the only variation is the corpus growing while the runs were going.

history.note: Fixed: turn-end reasons are an allowlist of abnormal endings.

title: every Session is told to read ~/.agents/USER_PREFERENCES.md, which exists in no checkout

evidence.excerpt: instructions.path-missing: ~/.dsh/AGENTS.md points at `~/.agents/USER_PREFERENCES.md`, which does not exist on this machine

rootCause: The instruction lives in the nixfiles-managed ~/.dsh/AGENTS.md and ~/.agents/AGENTS.md; the referenced asset is absent from ~/.config/nixfiles/assets/.agents/.
hypothesis: Creating the asset in nixfiles and mirroring it into ~/.agents/ removes one failed read from every Session.

history.note: Verified 2026-10-22: no USER_PREFERENCES reference remains in ~/.dsh/AGENTS.md or ~/.agents/AGENTS.md, and validate reports no instructions.path-missing finding. Fixed in nixfiles, not here.

title: apply_patch fails with "cannot get property workingDirectory without inject"

evidence.excerpt: Error: cannot get property "workingDirectory" without inject
Error: cannot get property "workingDirectory" without inject
Error: cannot get property "workingDirectory" without inject

rootCause: The tool handler reads context.workingDirectory off execution.agent.ctx (plugins/@dshfiles/apply-patch/src/patch-tool.ts:84). Cordis raises this error when the property is not provided by an inject declaration on the fiber that serves that ctx, so the plugin-level inject in host.ts does not reach the per-agent context the tool executes with.
hypothesis: Reading the service with a nullable lookup (ctx.get("workingDirectory")) or injecting it on the tool execution context removes 453 failures per week without changing patch semantics.

history.note: Root cause confirmed: the tool body resolved its context from execution.agent.ctx, and that scoped Agent context does not inject workingDirectory. Rebuilt the tool from the plugin context and register it from setup; regression test fails if the Agent context is read again.

title: bash calls over 30s grew 1,046 → 2,830 across 307 Sessions

evidence.excerpt: bash took 30s+ on 2 of 54 calls (worst 45.7s) (1046 → 2830 hits, 307 Sessions)

rootCause: Not established as a defect: a bash call over 30 s is the shape of a test run, a build or a blocking wait, and the tool has no timeout of its own. The 2026-10-24 review shows the growth, not its cause.
hypothesis: Most of the growth is long test/build commands and waits that belong in a background job; instruction-level guidance would move a minority, and a tool-level change is not justified without per-command attribution.

history.note: Measured as volume only, not attributed per command. Reopen when a review can attribute the slow calls by command family or job kind; then choose between guidance and a tool seam.

title: edit: "file has not been read" failures doubled to 315 while apply_patch was broken

evidence.excerpt: edit fails: Error: cannot modify "<path>@<path>": file has not been read — read the file, then retry (164 → 315 hits, 150 Sessions)

rootCause: Plausible, not proven: apply_patch (the tool built to remove this class by reading the file itself) failed on every call this window with the workingDirectory inject error, so agents fell back to edit and hit the read receipt. Same window, same direction: apply_patch 0 → 453, edit-not-read 164 → 315.
hypothesis: With apply_patch fixed, this class drops back toward the previous window without any change to edit or to the instructions. Next weekly review decides; no second intervention is started before that.

title: jj_thread_status called repeatedly with identical arguments: 61 → 176

evidence.excerpt: jj_thread_status called 4× with identical arguments — {} (61 → 176 hits, 27 Sessions)

rootCause: Uninvestigated. An identical repeated read inside one Session is the shape of a polling loop around a status the agent could wait for or cache, but writing the workspace status on every call is also correct after any mutation, so a naive cache would serve stale work.
hypothesis: A short single-flight window (identical arguments answered from the last result for a few seconds, invalidated by any of this workspace revision changes) removes the repeats without serving stale status.

title: opencode-go retries rose 13 → 239 (stream idle timeout)

evidence.excerpt: opencode-go-alex retried 2× (TIMEOUT: pi-ai stream idle timeout after 120000ms) (13 → 239 hits, 33 Sessions)

rootCause: Provider-side: 239 stream idle timeouts from one account route in the window is instability, not a harness defect, and the same route also timed out on quota reads.
hypothesis: Nothing to change in the harness; retry accounting already records it. Reopen only if the timeout rate survives an account or provider change.

history.note: Provider instability, not a harness cause. Reopen with evidence that a provider switch or a request-shape change removed it.
